what_its_for: Tralokinumab-ldrm is used to treat moderate-to-severe eczema (atopic dermatitis) in adults and children 12 years and older when other treatments have not worked well enough or cannot be used. It works by blocking a protein in your body that causes inflammation and itching in your skin.
how_to_take: This medicine is given as an injection under the skin (subcutaneous injection). Your doctor or nurse will give you the first injections in a clinic setting. After proper training, you or a caregiver may be able to give the injections at home. Common injection sites include the front of your thighs, your belly (abdomen, but not within 2 inches of your belly button), or the upper outer area of your arms (only if someone else is giving the injection). Rotate injection sites each time and never inject into skin that is red, bruised, tender, or affected by eczema. Let the pre-filled syringe or auto-injector sit at room temperature for about 30 minutes before injecting — do not warm it in a microwave or hot water. Check the liquid before use: it should be clear to slightly yellow and free of particles. Do not use if it looks cloudy or has visible particles.
dosing: For adults: The usual starting dose is 600 mg (given as two 300 mg injections at the same visit), followed by 300 mg every other week. After your eczema is well controlled, your doctor may reduce your dose to 300 mg once every 4 weeks. For adolescents (12–17 years): Dosing is based on body weight and will be determined by your doctor. Always follow your doctor's specific dosing instructions, as your dose may be different based on your individual situation.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, inject it as soon as you remember. Then, resume your regular dosing schedule from that point forward. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist. Do not inject a double dose to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store tralokinumab-ldrm in the refrigerator between 36°F and 46°F (2°C and 8°C). Keep it in the original carton to protect it from light. Do not freeze it, and do not use it if it has been frozen. If needed, you may store it at room temperature (up to 77°F / 25°C) for a maximum of 14 days. Once removed from the refrigerator, do not put it back. Discard it if not used within 14 days. Keep out of reach of children. Dispose of used syringes and auto-injectors in a proper sharps container — never throw them in regular household trash.
what_to_avoid: Do not receive live vaccines (such as live flu vaccine, MMR, chickenpox, or shingles vaccine) while using this medicine without talking to your doctor first, as it may not be safe. Talk to your doctor before starting any new vaccines. Do not share your injection device with anyone else. Avoid injecting into areas of skin that are sore, damaged, bruised, or affected by your eczema.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you experience: signs of a serious allergic reaction such as hives, rash, swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat, difficulty breathing, or dizziness; eye problems such as pink eye (conjunctivitis), eye redness, itching, or pain — these are relatively common side effects but should be evaluated; signs of infection such as fever, chills, or flu-like symptoms; pain, redness, swelling, or oozing at the injection site that does not go away. Call your doctor if your eczema does not seem to be improving after several weeks of treatment.
when_it_works: Most people begin to notice improvement in their skin within 2 to 4 weeks of starting treatment, but it may take up to 16 weeks to see the full benefit. Everyone responds differently, so give the medication time to work. Do not stop using it without talking to your doctor first, even if you do not see immediate results.
special_populations: Pregnancy: It is not fully known whether tralokinumab-ldrm is safe during pregnancy. Talk to your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. Breastfeeding: It is not known if this medicine passes into breast milk. Discuss the risks and benefits with your doctor before breastfeeding. Elderly (65 years and older): This medicine can be used in older adults; no dose adjustment is usually needed, but your doctor will monitor you closely. Children under 12 years: Safety and effectiveness have not been established in children under 12 years of age. Kidney or liver problems: No dose adjustment is typically required, but inform your doctor of any kidney or liver conditions.
